Do not flatten Pluto into generic transformation or give all outer planets the same big-transformation text. Hand sequence (not CORE): Uranus disrupts; Neptune dissolves distinction; Pluto makes the old model unviable and forces reconstruction.

Death-and-resurrection is symbolic, not a literal mortality prediction. Transpersonal power is not an automatic literal external-power event. Decay/corruption/death is Hand's lower register, not the complete meaning.

Decomposition→recombination is more precise than generic transformation. Reconstruction is incomplete without building a new workable everyday reality. Evolutionary Pluto is typically cumulative, not Uranian suddenness.

Helping others through transformation is paired with the ethical shadow: exploiting power gained through another's vulnerability. More precise than generic Pluto = manipulation. Cling-to-disintegrating-structure intensifies crisis.
Hand's psychotic-crisis / medication-suppression example is excluded from this ledger. Historical author remark in an astrology book, not a medically validated causal model, not runtime meaning.

claims.author: Robert Hand
claims.edition: Horoscope Symbols, 1981 Para Research / Schiffer ISBN 9780914918165
claims.locus: Ch.4 The Planets: Core Meanings — Pluto
claims.original_claim: Pluto symbolizes the end of the process begun by Uranus: the breaking apart of the reality-structure of ordinary consciousness.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto completes the Uranus-initiated disruption of ordinary reality by forcing radical reconstruction.

claims.author: Robert Hand
claims.edition: Horoscope Symbols, 1981 Para Research / Schiffer ISBN 9780914918165
claims.locus: Ch.4 The Planets: Core Meanings — Pluto
claims.original_claim: Pluto symbolizes the radical transformation of consciousness and being that results from this process.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto = radical transformation of consciousness/being after existing structures can no longer persist.

claims.author: Robert Hand
claims.edition: Horoscope Symbols, 1981 Para Research / Schiffer ISBN 9780914918165
claims.locus: Ch.4 The Planets: Core Meanings — Pluto
claims.original_claim: Pluto is the archetype of death and resurrection.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto theme: death-and-rebirth / ending followed by reconstitution.

claims.author: Robert Hand
claims.edition: Horoscope Symbols, 1981 Para Research / Schiffer ISBN 9780914918165
claims.locus: Ch.4 The Planets: Core Meanings — Pluto
claims.original_claim: Pluto breaks old and worn-out entities down into their component parts and reassembles them into a new being.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto mechanism: decomposition of obsolete structure → recombination into a new structure.

claims.author: Robert Hand
claims.edition: Horoscope Symbols, 1981 Para Research / Schiffer ISBN 9780914918165
claims.locus: Ch.4 The Planets: Core Meanings — Pluto
claims.original_claim: Where Uranus disrupts ordinary reality and Neptune disorients it by exposure to other realities, Pluto represents a total crisis of ordinary reality.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto = total crisis of an existing reality-model when that model can no longer remain viable.

claims.author: Robert Hand
claims.edition: Horoscope Symbols, 1981 Para Research / Schiffer ISBN 9780914918165
claims.locus: Ch.4 The Planets: Core Meanings — Pluto
claims.original_claim: The Plutonian crisis requires not merely confronting another reality but constructing a new everyday reality from it.
claims.normalized_claim: Constructive Pluto: build a new workable reality after the previous structure collapses.

claims.author: Robert Hand
claims.edition: Horoscope Symbols, 1981 Para Research / Schiffer ISBN 9780914918165
claims.locus: Ch.4 The Planets: Core Meanings — Pluto
claims.original_claim: Pluto operates with extreme power and, as an ego-transcending force, tends to be experienced as loss of control.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto theme: transpersonal/extreme power often experienced by the ego as loss of control.

claims.author: Robert Hand
claims.edition: Horoscope Symbols, 1981 Para Research / Schiffer ISBN 9780914918165
claims.locus: Ch.4 The Planets: Core Meanings — Pluto
claims.original_claim: Attempting to hold together what is disintegrating makes the Plutonian crisis harder and can frustrate the new birth.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto shadow: clinging to a structure that must end intensifies crisis and obstructs reconstruction.

claims.author: Robert Hand
claims.edition: Horoscope Symbols, 1981 Para Research / Schiffer ISBN 9780914918165
claims.locus: Ch.4 The Planets: Core Meanings — Pluto
claims.original_claim: Like Uranus and Neptune, Pluto requires detachment from what must disappear.
claims.normalized_claim: Constructive Pluto requires releasing attachment to structures whose cycle is ending.

claims.author: Robert Hand
claims.edition: Horoscope Symbols, 1981 Para Research / Schiffer ISBN 9780914918165
claims.locus: Ch.4 The Planets: Core Meanings — Pluto
claims.original_claim: Pluto represents an evolutionary power built into the nature of things.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto = intrinsic evolutionary process through development, decay, dissolution and reformation.

claims.author: Robert Hand
claims.edition: Horoscope Symbols, 1981 Para Research / Schiffer ISBN 9780914918165
claims.locus: Ch.4 The Planets: Core Meanings — Pluto
claims.original_claim: Unlike Uranus, Pluto's effects are not usually sudden because Pluto represents evolutionary power inherent in things.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto tempo: typically cumulative/evolutionary rather than characteristically sudden like Uranus.

claims.author: Robert Hand
claims.edition: Horoscope Symbols, 1981 Para Research / Schiffer ISBN 9780914918165
claims.locus: Ch.4 The Planets: Core Meanings — Pluto
claims.original_claim: Helping others through transformations is a constructive expression of Pluto.
claims.normalized_claim: Constructive Pluto: facilitate profound transformation in others.

claims.author: Robert Hand
claims.edition: Horoscope Symbols, 1981 Para Research / Schiffer ISBN 9780914918165
claims.locus: Ch.4 The Planets: Core Meanings — Pluto
claims.original_claim: Helping people in crisis creates power through knowledge of their vulnerabilities; exploiting that power for personal ends is dangerous.

claims.author: Robert Hand
claims.edition: Horoscope Symbols, 1981 Para Research / Schiffer ISBN 9780914918165
claims.locus: Ch.4 The Planets: Core Meanings — Pluto
claims.original_claim: Astrological literature emphasizes Pluto's associations with uncontrolled power, decay, corruption and death.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto shadow register: uncontrolled power, decay, corruption, destruction/death symbolism.

claims.author: Robert Hand
claims.edition: Horoscope Symbols, 1981 Para Research / Schiffer ISBN 9780914918165
claims.locus: Ch.4 The Planets: Core Meanings — Pluto
claims.original_claim: Pluto is also a purifying fire through which an entity passes from one level of being to another.
claims.normalized_claim: Constructive Pluto: purification through removal of obsolete/imperfect structure enabling transition to another level of being.

claims.author: Dane Rudhyar
claims.edition: New Mansions for New Men, Lucis Press 1938; Khaldea archival ed. 2008
claims.locus: Pt.2 Music of the Spheres — Pluto, Sower of Celestial Seed
claims.original_claim: Pluto is the Sower of Celestial Seed: the solar seed and, generally, the seeding process. In the seed rests the power of rebirth and the mystery of immortality.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto = sower of celestial seed: seeding-process that carries rebirth.

claims.author: Dane Rudhyar
claims.edition: New Mansions for New Men, Lucis Press 1938; Khaldea archival ed. 2008
claims.locus: Pt.2 Music of the Spheres — Pluto, Sower of Celestial Seed
claims.original_claim: Like the seed, Pluto is in the plant yet not of the plant. It belongs to the species and the new life to come, not to the particular plant that begins to die as the seed matures.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto is in the organism yet not of it: messenger of future life, not of the dying particular.

claims.author: Dane Rudhyar
claims.edition: New Mansions for New Men, Lucis Press 1938; Khaldea archival ed. 2008
claims.locus: Pt.2 Music of the Spheres — Pluto, Sower of Celestial Seed
claims.original_claim: Uranus transforms; Neptune dissolves and feeds prenatal growth; Pluto is the hierophant of the mysteries of actual birth into the New World.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto = hierophant of actual birth into the New World, not Uranus-transform or Neptune-dissolve.

claims.author: Dane Rudhyar
claims.edition: New Mansions for New Men, Lucis Press 1938; Khaldea archival ed. 2008
claims.locus: Pt.2 Music of the Spheres — Pluto, Sower of Celestial Seed
claims.original_claim: Whoever fails the Uranian tests is disintegrated by Neptune, and for such a one Pluto is the awesome lord of death. Who passes and enters the Neptunian Sea of Light is shown the gates of rebirth.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto shadow if Uranus fails: lord of death. If tests are passed: gates of rebirth.

claims.author: Dane Rudhyar
claims.edition: New Mansions for New Men, Lucis Press 1938; Khaldea archival ed. 2008
claims.locus: Pt.2 Music of the Spheres — Pluto, Sower of Celestial Seed
claims.original_claim: Immortality here is a generic fact and a process. Many seeds wither; Nature will not depend on the individual. The seeding process cannot be defeated even when particular seeds become manure.
claims.normalized_claim: Plutonian immortality is the seeding process, not a guarantee to the individual.

claims.author: Dane Rudhyar
claims.edition: New Mansions for New Men, Lucis Press 1938; Khaldea archival ed. 2008
claims.locus: Pt.2 Music of the Spheres — Pluto, Sower of Celestial Seed
claims.original_claim: The seed must descend into the depths. Christ and Orpheus descend to Hades; the male seed falls into the womb, the Hades-realm whence a new being arises after darkness.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto requires descent into depths/womb before arising as a new being.

claims.author: Dane Rudhyar
claims.edition: New Mansions for New Men, Lucis Press 1938; Khaldea archival ed. 2008
claims.locus: Pt.2 Music of the Spheres — Pluto, Sower of Celestial Seed
claims.original_claim: Pluto's orbit crossing inside Neptune's is cosmic fecundation: Plutonian seeds deposited in the Neptunian Sea of Light as womb. Pluto Father, Neptune Mother, Uranus Son.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto fecundates the Neptunian womb; Uranus is the child of that polarity.

claims.author: Dane Rudhyar
claims.edition: New Mansions for New Men, Lucis Press 1938; Khaldea archival ed. 2008
claims.locus: Pt.2 Music of the Spheres — Pluto, Sower of Celestial Seed
claims.original_claim: To God-in-the-Highest (the Sun) answers God-in-the-lowest (the seed). Seed-men demonstrate God in the deepest Earth-womb, farthest from sunrise.
claims.normalized_claim: Constructive Pluto: God-in-the-lowest — seed demonstrating divinity in the depths.

claims.author: Dane Rudhyar
claims.edition: New Mansions for New Men, Lucis Press 1938; Khaldea archival ed. 2008
claims.locus: Pt.2 Music of the Spheres — Pluto, Sower of Celestial Seed
claims.original_claim: The seed must die that the new plant may live. Seed-men sink into the matrix of futurity, thence to emerge as the new Life into which they died.
claims.normalized_claim: The seed dies into futurity so that the new plant may live.

claims.author: Dane Rudhyar
claims.edition: New Mansions for New Men, Lucis Press 1938; Khaldea archival ed. 2008
claims.locus: Pt.2 Music of the Spheres — Pluto, Sower of Celestial Seed
claims.original_claim: Pluto's message is divine substantiality: the Soul can be made substantial and concrete, not only a breath or astral vapor. Earth-substance and human souls can be regenerated.
claims.normalized_claim: Positive Pluto: Soul made substantial; earth-substance and souls regenerated.

claims.author: Dane Rudhyar
claims.edition: New Mansions for New Men, Lucis Press 1938; Khaldea archival ed. 2008
claims.locus: Pt.2 Music of the Spheres — Pluto, Sower of Celestial Seed
claims.original_claim: The God-seed is hidden in every man irrespective of birth-condition and environment. There can be no king where every man is king by divine right.
claims.normalized_claim: God-seed is in every person; not a privilege of birth or station.

claims.author: Dane Rudhyar
claims.edition: New Mansions for New Men, Lucis Press 1938; Khaldea archival ed. 2008
claims.locus: Pt.2 Music of the Spheres — Pluto, Sower of Celestial Seed
claims.original_claim: Pluto's Great Work is penetration of one's depths and revelation of oneself in every remotest part of one's being: to sow oneself into the farthest removes of one's earth.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto function: penetrate depths and reveal the self to itself in every part.

claims.author: Liz Greene
claims.edition: Living with Pluto, Campion interview, Mountain Astrologer Dec/Jan 2002; astro.com
claims.locus: astro.com in_plutint1_e.htm / in_plutint2_e.htm — Living with Pluto Parts 1–2
claims.original_claim: Matching Pluto to one archetype is artificial. Planetary symbols have family relations with many images; Plutonian ones include Lucifer, the Fates, Mephistopheles, and Kali.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto is a family of mythic images, not one boxed archetype.

claims.author: Liz Greene
claims.edition: Living with Pluto, Campion interview, Mountain Astrologer Dec/Jan 2002; astro.com
claims.locus: astro.com in_plutint1_e.htm / in_plutint2_e.htm — Living with Pluto Parts 1–2
claims.original_claim: The Pluto principle is almost only sayable in poetic metaphor: an intelligent life in substance itself, the life force in living nature that will survive.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto = life-force in nature/substance that persists.

claims.author: Liz Greene
claims.edition: Living with Pluto, Campion interview, Mountain Astrologer Dec/Jan 2002; astro.com
claims.locus: astro.com in_plutint1_e.htm / in_plutint2_e.htm — Living with Pluto Parts 1–2
claims.original_claim: To survive, that life force must go through permutations and death processes that break down forms past their time and then generate new forms.
claims.normalized_claim: Survival requires breaking down expired forms and generating new ones.

claims.author: Liz Greene
claims.edition: Living with Pluto, Campion interview, Mountain Astrologer Dec/Jan 2002; astro.com
claims.locus: astro.com in_plutint1_e.htm / in_plutint2_e.htm — Living with Pluto Parts 1–2
claims.original_claim: We experience Pluto as destructive (Mephistopheles), nourishing (Great Mother), or fate (Moirae), so several images are needed.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto has destructive, nourishing, and fateful registers — not one face.

claims.author: Liz Greene
claims.edition: Living with Pluto, Campion interview, Mountain Astrologer Dec/Jan 2002; astro.com
claims.locus: astro.com in_plutint1_e.htm / in_plutint2_e.htm — Living with Pluto Parts 1–2
claims.original_claim: Pluto feels so overwhelming that the common first response is to pull into Saturn and defend against it; that is natural, not necessarily best.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto overwhelm commonly triggers Saturnine self-defense.

claims.author: Liz Greene
claims.edition: Living with Pluto, Campion interview, Mountain Astrologer Dec/Jan 2002; astro.com
claims.locus: astro.com in_plutint1_e.htm / in_plutint2_e.htm — Living with Pluto Parts 1–2
claims.original_claim: Pluto is locked into a pattern of nature: a force that will either grind over everything or become the victim of everything.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto force: grind-over-all or become-victim-of-all.

claims.author: Liz Greene
claims.edition: Living with Pluto, Campion interview, Mountain Astrologer Dec/Jan 2002; astro.com
claims.locus: astro.com in_plutint1_e.htm / in_plutint2_e.htm — Living with Pluto Parts 1–2
claims.original_claim: Taken over, the attitude is life-or-death, win-or-be-destroyed; that drives power battles, manipulation, or arranging to be victimized by something powerful.
claims.normalized_claim: Shadow: life-or-death win/destruction lock — power-battle, manipulation, or victimization.

claims.author: Liz Greene
claims.edition: Living with Pluto, Campion interview, Mountain Astrologer Dec/Jan 2002; astro.com
claims.locus: astro.com in_plutint1_e.htm / in_plutint2_e.htm — Living with Pluto Parts 1–2
claims.original_claim: When being overpowered is too scary, especially with a fragile ego, people disconnect from feeling and start behaving like Pluto — obsessive.
claims.normalized_claim: Overwhelm plus disconnection can take the person over as obsessive Pluto-behavior.

claims.author: Liz Greene
claims.edition: Living with Pluto, Campion interview, Mountain Astrologer Dec/Jan 2002; astro.com
claims.locus: astro.com in_plutint1_e.htm / in_plutint2_e.htm — Living with Pluto Parts 1–2
claims.original_claim: You cannot manage Pluto without accepting something at work in life greater than yourself.
claims.normalized_claim: Constructive Pluto requires accepting a force greater than the personal self.

claims.author: Liz Greene
claims.edition: Living with Pluto, Campion interview, Mountain Astrologer Dec/Jan 2002; astro.com
claims.locus: astro.com in_plutint1_e.htm / in_plutint2_e.htm — Living with Pluto Parts 1–2
claims.original_claim: The survival instinct is a piece of raw nature in the individual; it comes out when the chips are down and personality is no longer relevant or is overwhelmed.
claims.normalized_claim: Pluto theme: survival instinct as raw nature when personality is overwhelmed.
